tables.how: The Department of Human Resources' table of permanent civil-service appointments (26,608 appointments since 15 October 2018) is joined to the City payroll on three things together: the appointee's name, the job class and the department, in the fiscal year of the appointment. 22,243 appointments match. Listed: the 3,290 whose appointee the payroll shows in the same class and department the fiscal year before with a type of appointment other than permanent civil service (1,922 temporary exempt, 930 permanent exempt, 438 provisional). 325 were the only appointment the table records from their eligible list and 683 were ranked first. The comparison: the other 18,953 matched appointments, of which 9,005 went to people not on the payroll the year before. The appointee is named on 2,072 rows, where the name is rare and has one spelling in the payroll; on the other 1,218 the name is too common to follow from one file to the other with confidence, so the row gives the appointment without it.
tables.limits: Moving temporary staff into permanent posts is something the City does openly: the civil grand jury recorded in 2023 that the City was converting temporary workers hired at the start of the pandemic into permanent civil-service workers, and a provisional appointee is by definition waiting for the examination. Experience in the job can fairly earn a high score. The question the figure raises is narrower: where the person was chosen first and the examination followed, was the examination open to others in practice? The table gives a rank and a list number but not how many people were on the list, whether the test was written for one position, or when the job was advertised. The fiscal year before is a coarse test: someone hired as a temporary and made permanent within the same fiscal year is not counted. Each row joins two public files by name, job class and department; it is not confirmed that the appointee and the person on the payroll the year before are one person. The appointment table has no police officer appointments and does not say how many people were on a list.

For each employee, class and year, regular salary is divided by hours paid (at least 1,040, half a year); overtime and “other” pay are left out, and because the hours include overtime hours the rate is if anything understated. That rate is compared with the highest step or range ceiling published for the class at any date up to the end of the fiscal year, including the extended steps that need special approval. An employee is listed when the rate is more than 25% above that ceiling and, where the class has five or more holders, more than 25% above the middle rate actually paid in the class, in at least two years. The “top of scale” column is the ceiling for the same number of hours. 314,765 employee-years could be compared; 7,839 were in classes with no published rate. tables.how: City payroll file, fiscal 2017 to 2026. A run is a set of consecutive fiscal years in which the same name is paid 1,040 hours or more (half time) in the same class and department with the employment type Temporary Exempt. Listed: every name, class and department with a run of four years or more: 816, of which 258 reach fiscal 2026. The last-but-one column marks the 740 counted on the narrower footing the case sets beside Human Resources' own reports (more than 1,040 hours, outside the transportation agency). The person is named on 560 rows, where the name is rare and has one spelling in the payroll; the other 256 are given by job class and department.
tables.limits: The civil grand jury wrote in 2023 that some temporary exempt workers may serve up to three years under what it called Category 18 of the Charter’s exemptions, and that the City gave pandemic hires a further year; the payroll does not say which category anyone is in, and other categories may carry other terms. A long run is therefore a question for the exempt-appointment reports, not a breach shown by the payroll. Some classes are set up as temporary: in fiscal 2026 the payroll shows 100.0% of the hours in the largest group here, Special Nurse (class P103), as temporary exempt, which points to a standing as-needed class rather than a time-limited post. Two people with one name in the same class and department would be counted as one. What Human Resources itself reports as past the limit is in the list of exempt appointments past their limit. The analysis counted these runs by class and department and did not list individuals; each row here is the same count made visible, and a run under one name is not confirmed to be one person.

tables.how: A snapshot of the City careers site taken on 14 November 2026: every listed posting with its posting date, appointment type, job class and the filing deadline as printed. Days open is the printed deadline minus the posting date; where the wording is “on or after” a date, that date is the earliest the posting can close. Postings with no date in the deadline text are counted but not measured. Holders is the number of people paid in the class citywide in fiscal 2026. Shortest first. Civil Service Rule 110 requires examination announcements to be posted for a minimum period “not to be less than three (3) business days”. All 182 postings are listed, the 94 with a measurable deadline first, shortest first; the rest have no closing date or none that can be read.
tables.limits: One day’s snapshot cannot show the past: nothing on disk says how long the posting ran for any job already filled, and the careers site keeps no archive. A short posting must meet the three-business-day minimum, and exempt posts are not examinations, so that rule may not reach them at all. A posting dated late on one day in universal time can be a day earlier in San Francisco, and the date is the one the page carries now, so a posting that was re-issued or extended shows its latest date and can look shorter than it was. A short window narrows who can apply; it does not show that a candidate was chosen beforehand. The recruitment file for each posting would show how many applied.

tables.how: Position lists of the 12 enacted Annual Salary Ordinances on disk, each of which covers two fiscal years; the first-year figure of the later ordinance is taken as the enacted count for a year. Paid full-time equivalents are hours paid divided by the paid hours of a full-time year in that fiscal year, read off the file (2,080 in most years, 2,160 in fiscal 2026), from the City payroll, fiscal 2017 to 2026, for rows whose type of appointment is permanent civil service, permanent exempt or provisional; temporary exempt and other rows are shown separately, beside the ordinance’s own lines for temporary staff, which are not job classes and are left out of the position count. Ordinance department codes are matched to the payroll’s. “Never filled” counts a class in a department authorized at one position or more in each of the last five years with no hours paid in it there in any of them; “paid above” counts a class paid at least three full-time equivalents and half as much again above its authorized count. Listed: all 84 lines never paid in five years and all 20 paid above their count, largest first within each kind.
tables.limits: The two lists often mirror each other: a department authorized for one class pays people in a neighbouring class instead, which the ordinance allows as a temporary substitution. A line left empty for five years can also be a class kept for grant money that did not arrive, or a line whose department code differs between the two files. The position-control record, which ties each person to a position number, would settle each line; it is not published. The ordinances whose first year is fiscal 2016 and 2019 are scans whose department totals reconcile only in part, so those years’ counts are approximate. The ordinances print no flags for new, substituted or deleted positions, and mid-year amendments are not on disk. A gap is not waste in itself: budgets assume some posts stay vacant, a post can be held by someone paid in a lower or different class while it is being filled, and hours fall short of 2,080 for anyone who started or left during the year. Those same substitutions are why a class can be paid above its count.

rows.quote: “selection of employees from eligible lists shall be based on merit”

rows.document: Time to Get to Work: San Francisco’s Hiring Crisis
rows.said: The civil grand jury found that the median time to fill a City job was 255 days, more than three times the figure reported for San Mateo County, and that hiring can take more than 50 steps.
rows.quote: “time it takes the City to fill a job is 255 days”

rows.document: Public Integrity Review - San Francisco Department of the Environment's Relationship with Recology and Lack of Compliance with Ethics Rules
rows.said: The Controller found that two employees of Recology sat on at least six of the Environment Department’s job recruitments in five years, and that no City rule stops an interested party sitting on a hiring panel, although Civil Service Rule 113.1.2 bars selection by nepotism or favoritism.
rows.quote: “cannot be based on non-merit based factors such as nepotism or favoritism”

rows.document: Public Integrity Investigation at the Department of Building Inspection (City Attorney report, January 18, 2022)
rows.said: The City Attorney found that the Building Inspection Commission itself promoted a deputy director, an appointment normally made by the director, then made him director, while the outgoing director stayed on in a temporary post as Special Assistant to the Director.
rows.quote: “promoted Hui as Deputy Director through a very unusual process”

rows.document: Public Integrity Review: Preliminary Assessment - Department of Building Inspection's Permitting and Inspections Processes
rows.said: The Controller wrote that the former Building Inspection director gained personally from preferential treatment he allowed, which may have helped his job security and benefitted his relatives through City hiring.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance Audit of the Ethics Commission
rows.said: The budget analyst noted that permanent civil-service posts are filled through an open and competitive examination, which permanent exempt appointments do not require, and that the Ethics Commission’s median time from posting to hire was 160 days.
rows.quote: “which is not required for PEX positions”

Each row gives the publisher’s date, a one-sentence summary, a quotation of at most twelve words checked against the stored text, and the link recorded when the document was downloaded.
tables.limits: These are findings about particular departments in particular years, several of them about people who have since left; they are not findings about anyone named in the other lists. Two rows are whistleblower summaries, which do not name the department. A short quotation cannot carry a report’s reasoning: read the page it comes from.
